summary: Phase 2 (Credit Lending + Resource Allocation) full test. Backend: new suite tests/test_phase2_lending_allocation.py covering JRN-19..50, Q-8 and Q-9. 21/21 pass. reconcile.py prints ALL OK before and after every action sequence. Phase 1 regression (JRN-51): 43/44 pass. The 1 failure comes from leftover test data that E1 did not clean up, not from a code bug. Frontend (Playwright): JRN-19/20/21/25/28/29/30/34 desktop, Q-10 at 390px (Maya requests from Tomás -> switch to Tomás, accept -> Maya repays (over-repay shows an inline error) -> Tomás confirms -> Repaid), Q-11 disclaimers, REQ-41 Overview panel updates after accept (880->890 available, 250->260 borrowed), View-as 'Individual friends' group, login shows only the 4 demo buttons. Allocation UI checked for Admin, Manager and Employee: budget errors, suggestion 'Review & apply' prefill, reallocate persists after reload, partial approve 300 moves the pool 1000->700, req_001 then fails with 'Not enough unallocated department budget', reject note visible to Arjun, employee cancel, 390px with no horizontal scroll, dialogs fit. Q-8 passes for the same entry/request (5/5 trials each: exactly [200,409], balance changes once). A probe found a real race on DIFFERENT entries/requests (see critical issues).

critical.issue: TOCTOU race. The pool check (dept budget − allocated) runs before the conditional status update, and the allocation $inc is unconditional. Approving two DIFFERENT pending requests in parallel (750 each, pool 1000) returned [200,200] in 2/3 trials. Pool became −500 and reconcile.py printed 'FAIL Engineering: member allocations 20500 exceed budget'. I restored the data afterwards.

TOCTOU race. The lender's available is checked in balances() before the transition, with no lock or reservation. Kwame (available 83) accepted two different 62-credit requests in parallel: 1/3 trials gave [200,200] and his available went to −41, so the 'Not enough available credits to lend' rule was bypassed. Same risk on POST /lending/offers and when repayments are recorded in parallel (outstanding − awaiting is checked non-atomically; only confirm is guarded by $expr).

minor.issue: Only the department manager is notified. Admins got the 'allocation.request' notification on create but not on cancel.
Same check-then-write pattern (dept_allocated is computed and then written, non-atomically). Low impact but the same race class.
req_001 urgency is 'normal' in the DB but 'high' in seed.py. The seed is insert-if-missing, so the DB has drifted from the current seed definition.

issues: Due date uses the browser's native <input type=date> instead of a shadcn Calendar/Popover date picker
Urgency options are lowercase (low/normal/high). Capitalise the labels.
The 'X / mo' sub-label under Allocation wraps onto 2 lines ('3,500 /' then 'mo'). The column is too narrow.

action_items: Make approve_request atomic against the department pool: e.g. a per-department lock/counter document with a conditional $inc (allocated + n <= budget), or a Mongo transaction. Re-run tests/race_probe.py; reconcile must stay ALL OK.

Make lending accept/offer atomic against the lender's available: e.g. a per-user reservation/lock doc, or reserve 'lent_outstanding' on a balance doc with a conditional $inc. Also guard record_repayment against parallel over-recording.

Clean up the leftover test user from E1's own testing: usr_5d50cd4f7417 (t_d5b361@example.com, 'TEST Friend'), its friendship with Maya, lending entries lnd_b3b6cfda9925, lnd_c1372f75535b, lnd_1eab8425a79c and their repayments. They show in Maya's demo Lending page and friends list, and they break tests/test_phase1_round2.py::TestLending::test_maya_ledger, which asserts exactly 4 entries. Alternatively, relax that assertion to a subset check.
Notify admins on request cancel too (optional).
Use a shadcn Calendar for the due date; capitalise urgency labels.
critical_code_review_comments: services/allocation.py approve_request: pool check -> _decide -> _inc_alloc. Between the check and the inc, other approvals can consume the pool. _decide only protects the same request.
services/lending.py respond(accept) and create_entry(offer): available is computed from aggregate reads, then the status flips. Nothing serialises per lender.

services/lending.py record_repayment: the awaiting sum and the insert are not atomic. Two parallel 60-credit records on 60 outstanding both get inserted (confirm is still guarded by $expr, so the data stays consistent but the UX is confusing).

Positive: conditional find_one_and_update gives a correct single 409 for double actions. RBAC scoping is correct (party_entry 403, manager dept scoping, require_module/require_org). Exact REQ error copy matches. History/notify/audit are written for every action.

success_rate.backend: 100% of the Phase 2 suite (21/21). Phase 1 regression 43/44 (data pollution). 2 race-condition defects found by the probe

The reallocate dialog error testid is field-error-realloc-credits. The resource-request dialog error testids are field-error-request-amount/-reason.
rca of the issue: Race: the invariant checks (pool >= n, lender available >= credits) read aggregates computed across several documents, then write in a separate operation. MongoDB single-document atomicity only covers the request/entry status flip, so concurrent actions on different documents both pass the check. Repro: python tests/race_probe.py (2/3 runs violated the invariants). Mitigation: serialise per department/lender with a lock document (find_one_and_update with a conditional on the counter) or a multi-document transaction, and re-verify after the write.
